utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Lausic, I would again like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Misetic will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before we pick up where we left off yesterday, I'd like to ask you a question about your meeting with Brian Foster on Sunday. I believe you mentioned that Mr. Foster gave you some documents on Sunday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me where this meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hotel where I'm accommodated, in the lobby.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me how long the meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handing over the documents was very brief. It was only a technical matter. There was no explanation as to what it was about, but then we spent a pleasant hour chatting about our experiences in the police, our respective experiences in our previous lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the course of this conversation, did the topic of your status in this case, or your status generally, I should say, whether you were a suspect or witness, was that discussed at all during that conversation?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not once.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did -- was there any conversation about why the OTP wanted to videotape or tape, I should say, an interview with you last week?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Not for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, finally, did you have any conversations with anyone who offered you an explanation as to why your conversation was being video-taped? I should say taped. I'm saying video-taped. I mean audio- or video-taped.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be precise about the time you're referring to. When would I have had a conversation about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At any time during or after the time you were asked to sit with the Office of the Prosecutor for another meeting in January of 2009, did anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor or your attorney tell you why your interview with them was going to be taped?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for the 20th of January, as I stated on the first day, in a telephone conversation through an interpreter with Mr. Foster.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I was a bit confused if you look at your screen, page 2, line 17. It gave the impression as if the conversation on that Sunday was taped. It says, "was taped" instead of later you used different language. You said at a later stage, you said, "was going to be," whereas, in this line, you say, "was video-taped." So I was a really confused about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the fact that, Mr. Lausic, was supposed to be interviewed last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. I'm not a native-speaking person I was confused by that language. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Finally, during this conversation with Mr. Foster, did you have any conversation about the subject of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this meeting on Sunday, in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no not for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Referring to your diary, which is P2166 - we don't need it on the screen, Mr. Registrar - just some background questions. Mr. Lausic, do you have the original version of your diary with you?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you have the ability to get it, in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Zagreb, I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How did you go about giving your diary to the Office of the Prosecutor? Did you give the diary to them directly?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When preparing for my suspect interview in May 2004, I had some 20 days to prepare, and this diary, or, actually, my work book, which I've been keeping continually, and I still do, I make a note of my daily activities; and that's an aide-memoire I used to remind myself of the times and events to be discussed at the interview. As in that diary, as you call it, there are also personal notes which refer neither to my activities in the Ministry of Defence or any other official business, but purely personal matters. Whatever in that diary referred to my activities as chief of the military police, all the meetings, contacts, and other notes concerning those duties, I copied and I had it certified so that at the interview in May 2004, I showed this to the investigators. Then they asked me to sign, which I did, that the copy was faithful to the contents of my original diary, and this is the material that is in the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, would you be willing to provide us with the copy of the original diary, at least for the relevant time-period that we're talking about here; let's say, for 1995?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more precise as to what from the copies should be photocopied and delivered to you? You can make your request, and I will mark the parts that are personal. But whatever has been copied, I can photocopy in the original and submit to you or to any of your colleague, either in the Defence or in the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President I propose that if we can towards the end of this session or beginning of the next talk about it outside the presence of the witness, but I don't want to spend time on it right now, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems okay to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One final question on your diary, was it -- did you ever turn over your original diary to any institution of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody ever asked me to, except in August, when I had an interview with the investigators as a witness in connection with Operation Medacki Dzep, and where I was on particular dates and these are matters I couldn't recollect during the interview in May; so I brought along the original diary and showed them the relevant pages; and that's how they were able to check that the copy I had given them was correct. But they didn't ask me to hand it over to them, nor did I ever hand it over to anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Hopefully the real final question on this topic. Did you ever feel obligated under Croatian law to turn the diary over?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I'm not aware of the relevance this has to this particular proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think it is highly relevant to the proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps not a matter to be discussed in the presence of the witness. I must -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We can save the discussion for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the end of the break. At the end, just before the break, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar if we can now turn your attention to matters that we left off yesterday. Mr. Registrar, if I could have 1D66-0153, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, if you look on the cover page here - this is not in your binder, I'm pretty sure - this is a systemisation of work posts in the military police administration. The proponent is you, and it was approved by the minister of defence, and the date is November 1994. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page in English, and I believe it is page 9 in the Croatian. Yeah, it's number 1, right. Item number 1 on the systemisation. Page 2, yes. Okay. Sorry, it's page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lausic, at item number 1 it's the job description for the chief of the military police administration, and in the job description that you wrote, it says: "Responsible for the work of the MP administration and MP units, and commands and controls MP units of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia." Now, you drafted this in November 1994, but it was also true in August of 1995 that you were responsible for the work of the MP administration and the military police units; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with Article 8 of the rules of the organisation and the work of the military police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So I'm correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I know what it said here in 1994. I'm saying that was the case in August of 1995 as well. You were responsible for the work of the MP administration and the MP units; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is valid until it is rendered null and void and until a new systemisation is adopted. To the best of my knowledge, in 1995, we did not adopt a new systemisation, so this one was still in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'd like to turn your attention, if we could go in the English to page 28, please, which is item number 35. I think it is also page 28 in the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 17 in the Croatian, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll wait for the English to come up as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the job descriptions for the military police crime investigation department, and for the chief of the MP crime investigation department, the description is: "Analyses and observes emergent forms of criminal behaviour and plans operative, preventative, and repressive measures in view of preventing criminal behaviour; organises and leads the entire work of the crime investigation MP of the Republic of Croatia. He is responsible for the activity of the crime investigation military police regarding crime prevention within the jurisdiction of the military court; provides expert help and directly participates in most complex actions and processing activities." And finally: "He organises the coordinated work with other security elements within the security system of the Republic of Croatia." Now you have said already that this was in effect in 1995. Do you recall who the chief of the MP crime investigation department was in August 1995. If you could hold your answer. Mr. Lausic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the chief of the crime investigation military police department in August 1995 was Major Spomenko Eljuga, but I can't be absolutely sure of that, although I think I'm right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could go to page 33 in the English and page 20 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, within the crime -- the military police crime investigation department, there were various sections; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you look at page -- at the screen in front of you, there's a description for the head of the section for the prevention of criminal offences against general safety, and you can look at his job description: "Analyses and observes emergent forms of criminal behaviour related to general safety; plans the carrying out of operative, preventative, and repressive measures and actions aimed at the prevention of this form of criminal behaviour; subordinate to the department chief of the crime investigation military police in matters regarding the prevention of criminal offences against general safety in the territory of the Republic of Croatia." Do you recall who the head of the section for prevention of criminal offences against general safety was in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't be precise, and I don't wish to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall if it may have been Ante Glavan?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a possibility, but I can't be precise. Forty years have passed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Fourteen, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in terms of subordination, the head of the prevention of the section for prevention of general offences is subordinated to the chief of the crime investigation MP, who is then subordinated to whom?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, as the chief of the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now was it the same organisational structure within the battalions themselves? In other words, there was within the battalions a chief of the crime investigation section and then within that section of the battalions, were there separate -- I'm sorry, the crime investigation sector and then separate sections within the crime investigation sector?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I -- in the same way that I have the systemisation on the screen, could I please have the establishment manual of a battalion on the screen? And then I can tell you for certain. There was always a section of the crime police, but I can't be precise about its structure, numbers and so on. But since have you the systemisation, you can also have the establishment manual put up on the screen, and then I can be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if necessary, I will retrieve that but for right now, I think we will have plenty of documents to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this exhibit into evidence, which is 1D66-0153.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become exhibit D1284.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I could have 1D66-0153, please. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for clarification, I understood that Mr. Misetic was referring to the systemisation of work posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So did I it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which seems to be 1D66-0182, according to the copy that was distributed to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That can't be because I'm looking at the -- might be the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's right. And actually we need to be careful with that because I noticed that problem from yesterday's transcript and documents as well so this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The original is always the one we call up with the 1D number, the translation not, so that is the practice we have been using throughout the trial. Now, Mr. Registrar, if we could have Exhibit D409, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lausic, this is the exhibit that we discussed or you discussed under examination by Mr. Tieger. Discussed that Minister Susak said the military police must be more energetic in its actions and prevent all offences, but I'd like to call your attention to page 6 in the English. And -- I'll wait for the Croatian version, which is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Page 4 in the Croatian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down to the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your notes indicate at 1730 that there was meeting where Minister Susak, Minister Jarnjak, Assistant Minister of the MUP, Mr. Moric, and - if we could turn the page, please - obviously you as the person taking notes were present. What was the purpose of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to make a correction. I did not keep notes for the purposes of the meeting. I was keeping my notes in my work book. I was not the person who was supposed to keep a record of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I was suggesting was even though your name doesn't appear there, that's because these are your notes, and so you wouldn't have put your own name as being present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page in Croatian, please, and one back in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, again, my question was: What was the purpose of the meeting that was held at 1730 hours on the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, the letters are too small. I would like to refer to my paper copies. It is difficult for me to follow on the screen. I don't have the right glasses for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does Mr. Tieger might know where the entry in his book is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, I just don't know how it's organised. I think the witness would probably have a better idea about that at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, I will do my best. I can see better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just without -- Mr. Lausic, let me before we start reading the notes, we can read the notes. I'm just asking, generally speaking, do you have a recollection of why that meeting was called?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was invited by Minister Susak to go to his office where I found Mr. Jarnjak and his assistant, Mr. Moric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And when you arrived, what did you come to learn was the purpose of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, the first note says Minister Susak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, no. As I said, we can read the notes, but what is the purpose of the meeting? Was it to coordinate the work of the military and civilian police?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if you see what Minister Jarnjak --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll to the bottom in the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Or Minister Jarnjak right above the entry for 1815. Now, Minister Jarnjak says women and children in one group and men to reception centres in the zones of each of the six police administrations. And yesterday we saw that you had issued an order about where women and children were supposed to be taken. Was your order about where to take women and children based on what was discussed at this meeting at 1730, on the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also have to remind you, that after this meeting, on the 3rd of August, in the Ministry of Interior, there was a coordination meeting of the civilian and military police at the highest level, where that was one of the topics that was discussed. The conclusion of the meeting is what I translated into my order to the military police as to how to treat the civilians. It was expected that in the area of combat that that area will be abandoned by the civilians residing there moving towards the free territory. Some reception had to be organised in accordance with the instructions provided. Women and children, as well as the elderly were supposed to be taken as one group, and men separated to another, and then processed in order to establish whether they participated in any combat against the Republic of Croatia. It was expected that in the combat area the civilians residing there would begin leaving it, moving towards the free areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this coordination meeting that took place on the 3rd, was that something that was also discussed at this meeting on the 2nd. In other words, was there a discussion at the meeting between Minister Jarnjak and Minister Susak about the fact that there should be a coordination meeting the next day between you and Mr. Moric and your associates?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting with Minister Susak was a brief one. I don't think it lasted for more than half an hour. And then Mr. Moric and I agreed to meet the next day. If you follow it up, you will see that at 6.15 p.m., I held a collegium meeting of the MP administration, whereupon I conveyed to my associates the information of that day. I also told them that we were to meet the next day in the Ministry of Interior with our colleagues from that ministry. That was the further development.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually I wanted to go next to the meeting at 1815 the collegium, and the first entry in your notes is: "Till now there has been a discrepancy between the orders decided and the working meetings held and the way in which these orders have been executed in the field." It says: "Not energetic enough in approach." The entry: "Not energetic enough in approach," it somewhat calls to mind Minister Susak's earlier comment in the day that the military police must be more energetic in its actions. And then it says you've identified three teams, the third of which is the team Split, team leader Major Juric. Now these teams, they were created precisely because as you state initially in your notes for 1815 that there was a problem between the content of the orders and the execution in the field. And you wanted these teams to be able to actually fully execute the orders as you were issuing them; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. At the beginning of the collegium meeting, after I briefed the chiefs of departments and sections, I pointed out the conclusions after the analysis which followed Operation Flash in May that year. I reminded them of the facts we established during that analysis. That is also somewhere in the documents that I received as a copy of my diary. The basis of it was that when personally observing Operation Flash in May 1995 and when touring the field, I noticed that the military policemen involved as well as their commanders were not sufficiently energetic in certain situations; when they came across HV members while looting, or breaching discipline in other ways. I noticed that their tactics and methodology was lacking, and that they were not economising with the resources and personnel that they had. On the basis of those conclusions which we drafted together after the analysis of Operation Flash and the participation of the military police in it, I decided, given the scope of Operation Storm and the area it was to encompass, and given the larger figures of HV and military police members who were to participate in it, to establish three forward command posts of the military police. The first forward command post was to be located with the Military District forward command post in Ogulin; then in Sisak, that is the military district of Zagreb; and the third one was in Sajkovici where there was the forward command post of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could now turn to D267. I don't want to go through this again. We've seen it twice, I think. But this is the order, again, of the 2nd, about preparations and this is the order - if we go to paragraph 10, which is page 4 in the English -- page 5, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, I'm sorry, it's page 4, paragraph 10, page 2 in the Croatian. If we could turn the page in Croatian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is again the order where you appoint, formally appoint Major Juric and you write that: "The commanders of the 72nd VP Battalion and 73rd VP Battalion shall be subordinated to Major Ivan Juric." This was that -- let me ask you first this question. This order, was it written after the meeting at 1815, after the collegium?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. However, the order on dispatching Major Juric to the forward command post of the MP administration is a separate order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I got that as well, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that separate order, we see Major Juric's tasks defined. It is also mentioned, therein, that Major Juric, within the system of command, is superior to the commander of the 72nd and the 73rd Battalion of the military police in that part of the tasks which have to do with the assistance provided to the 72nd Battalion by the 73rd Battalion of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that document. But first I want to take you to P2172, please. And if you scroll -- this is the order that appointed Colonel Kozic to head the IZM forward command post in Ogulin for the Main Staff. As we can see in paragraph 1, it was issued on the 2nd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn the page and scroll down in the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just want you to note that terms of the tasks that you defined for Colonel Kozic, it says: "With regard to daily operations command, he is subordinate to the Main Staff forward command post commander in Ogulin."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could go to Exhibit D268, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is the order that you were referring to earlier. And if we look -- if we turn the page - this is also the 2nd of August - we can actually leave it right there, I'm sorry, in the English. It says -- here's where you appoint a group of military police administration officers led by Major Ivan Juric including the following officers, then you name them. From the general VP department Mr. Muduna and then senior-lieutenant Ante Glavan. And I asked you before do you recollect that Mr. Glavan was, in fact, at that time the section chief for the prevention of criminal offences against general safety. You recalled appointing him as the section chief to go down with Major Juric's team?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that is correct. I said I could not recall who the chief of section for the prevention of crimes directed at endangering general safety was. I remember Mr. Glavan, but as for whether he was the chief of the section, that I don't know. This was a mixed team headed by Major Juric. I can see from here that there was someone from the crime police, traffic police, as well as regular duty police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But you do remember that Mr. Glavan was from the crime police section; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could, in the English, turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now you write: "In the command system he is superior to the commanders of the 72nd and 73rd with regard to the 73rd extending assistance to the 72nd Battalion?" And then the next entry is: "He is responsible for the implementation of all military police tasks in the 72nd Military Police Battalion zone of responsibility?" What that language means is that he is responsible for all -- for the tasks that are defined in Article 10 of the 1994 rules; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All tasks relating to the scope of work of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which, again, if you disagree with me, let me know; but I think you've said already is defined in Article 10 of the rules; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you also say: "He shall cooperate and coordinate nature the implementation of tasks with the workers of Zadar-Knin police administration, the Split Military District assistant for SIS chief of the SIS centre in Split, and HV commanders in the Split Military District, and north operative group zones of responsibility." Now, again, is this horizontal coordination between Mr. Juric and the various other branches of the Croatian government that you have specified in that order?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? Is your question whether that model functioned, or something else? You're asking me whether Major Juric indeed implemented the tasks referred to in the order, or are you asking me something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me put it a different way. Major Juric was supposed to coordinate with commanders of the Split Military District; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the commanders of the Croatian army, within the area of responsibility of the Split Military District, and the Operational Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Operational Sector North the reason it adds that is because that Operational Sector North at that time was in Bosnia at that time; correct? Yes. Have you to --

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next entry you have is: "He authorised to undertake all measures to ensure efficient and effective implementation of military police tasks in the 72nd Military Police and north operative zone -- operative group zones of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then the reporting shall be pursuant to a separate order that you had issued which we've seen before that reports had to go at 8.00 p.m. to you; correct? One more point on this document. You copied the Split Military District commander on this order, so he should have been informed about what you were instructing Major Juric to do; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from the document that it was indeed sent to the commander of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you subordinate for daily operational purposes Major Juric the way you subordinated for daily operational purposes Mr. Kozic to the commander of the Main Staff forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, and its forward command post in Ogulin, did not comprise any military police, unlike other Military Districts. It was for that reason why I appointed him to the forward command post of the Main Staff. There were Main Staff officers who, operatively speaking, did not have any subordinated MP battalions. That is why I appointed Major Kozic to that forward command post and subordinated him to the commander of the forward command post of the Main Staff. You can also see from the document that he was superior to the commanders of the 70th and 71st Battalion. Those were the battalions of the Military Districts of Gospic and Karlovac. Major Kozic was sent to the forward command post of the Main Staff because there was no MP battalion there. And Major Juric was sent to the forward command post of the military police attached to the forward command post of the Split Military District, which had its own 72nd MP Battalion. The same order applied to Major Cvitanovic, who was at Sisak, the forward command post of the Zagreb Military District, which had its own 67th MP Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was the intention to give the Main Staff forward command post the ability to utilise major Kozic in the event they needed military police assistance?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To shorten the communication path, had I not done that, the commander of the forward command post of the Main Staff would have to communicate through the Main Staff in Zagreb, and then to reach me in the end. This way, we had an officer from the MP administration with the authorities delegated by me. Since he was subordinated to the commander of the forward command post of the Main Staff, he could deal with the problems that had to do with MP police tasks immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So is it correct then, based on that answer, that General Gotovina could go to Mr. Budimir for daily operational tasks, but that if he wanted to get to Major Juric, it would have had to go through you, in the military police administration, send a request, and then have you send an order to Major Juric; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was the commander of the 72nd Battalion, who in terms of daily operational command was subordinated to him, and he could use the commander of the 72nd Battalion, and then through Major Juric, to ask for assistance from the MP administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is stated --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's not what I am saying. Not that he wants to seek assistance from the MP administration, but rather, to put it simply, General Gotovina can't issue an order to Major Juric?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's -- I just want to draw a line. The witness was completing his answer. The -- the intervention by counsel was not for the purpose of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- sort of stopping an answer that was not responsive but instead disputing the answer. And the answer needs to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think have you given us clear instructions, it's page 15295 lines 18 to 24. If there's anything that he thinks that I haven't clarified with the witness, he is free to do it in redirect. My question was not - and I think he was confused - how to get assistance from the military police administration which is evident as to what he was getting at. My question was the opposite, which was to get assistance from Major Juric, and that's what I want to focus on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, if Mr. Misetic has serious reasons to believe that the witness misunderstood his answer then he is entitled to put it again. Could you please repeat your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will be very precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think my last -- the way I rephrased the question is precise. Pursuant to the order appointing Major Juric, General Gotovina doesn't have the authority to issue him a direct order; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But through the commander of the 72nd Battalion, as mentioned in Article 12 of the order, under preparation of the units of the MP, to carry out police tasks which we saw on the screen. In item 12, which mentions the system of command and reporting in the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the following: "All requests and needs from the administration of the military police, the commander is referring to the MP commanders, should request these through the officer of the military police. Those other commanders of the forward command posts of the military police administration except for the 66th MP and the 74th Battalion" -- or, rather: "Company of the military police attached to the air force, who submit requests directly." So the commander of the 72nd Battalion was authorised through Juric to submit all requests concerning reinforcement, replenishment, equipment and so on. This was the usual way in which requests were sent to the MP administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That all may be true, Mr. Lausic. That has nothing to do with what I asked you, however. Just to follow up on that point. There would be no reason for General Gotovina to issue a request for more people for Mr. Juric to use; right? If Mr. Juric wanted more people, Mr. Juric would ask you directly. He doesn't need to wait for General Gotovina to tell him that he should request from you more personnel.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different people can see the same situation differently. It depends on how each one assesses the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand that answer, but ... Let's move on. Mr. Glavan was part of this forward command post that you set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we can go, Mr. Registrar, to P979 please. Now, this is a document authored by Ante Glavan. And if we can go to the end to assist Mr. Lausic first and then we'll come back to the end of the document. I'm sorry, to the signature page. And one back in the Croatian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you see the signature of Ante Glavan and he signed it department chief.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a little, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's all right now. Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection that, in fact, Mr. Glavan was the section chief, or department chief, I should say?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently, as it's in the signature. But here you can see that somebody signed it for Mr. Ante Glavan. This is not actually his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we can go back to the first page please. Actually you can also note there is no courtesy copy there, I hope you saw, to the Split Military District Command. Now it is send to the military police crime investigation department, stand-in-chief, Captain Spomenko Eljuga. And the subject is report on activities undertaken by the military crime police for 12 August 1995 at 8.30. Then it goes through, and we won't take up a lot of court time with this, but the document basically talks about the different processing of prisoners of war that was taking place in the various companies on the ground. You'll - as I said - note that this report only goes to Mr. Eljuga. And then if we can then take a look and see some of Mr. Eljuga's report. But, again, this is Mr. Glavan while he was still working in the forward command post in the Split Military District. If we can go to D852, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is for 5 August, and I know the font is small, Mr. Lausic, so we'll try to blow that up for you. This is it Mr. Eljuga's report within the military police administration. It is his operative report on the 5th of August. Now, who is this report being prepared for? To whose attention?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that he addressed it to Colonel Ivanovic, an officer from the military police administration. Maybe the heading is on the second page at the end, where all the addressees are listed. And it says in the title: Action return.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, what was action return?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it referred to the return of our refugees who had fled from the areas which were now liberated, but I'm not absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now is it -- and you can flip through it if you wish. This is it Mr. Eljuga putting together the various reports from the crime sections in the various forward command posts, putting them in one report within the military police administration; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to read it very carefully to understand what it's about and confirm or not confirm what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But let me see if you agree with me. Mr. Glavan who was sent as part of Mr. Juric's team as a crime military police officer would report to Mr. Eljuga and then Mr. Eljuga -- who was in Zagreb; correct? Mr. Eljuga would have been in Zagreb at that time?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But can we please go back to Mr. Glavan's report, and on the second page, you can see that he delivered the same report to the chief of the department of the crime military police of the 72nd Battalion. He sent them a copy. If you go back to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct. But the crime police section chief then would report up his chain of command, up to the crime section, if necessary, in Zagreb; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's the vertical line, along the professional line, and he also sent it to the -- his professional line of the 72nd Battalion, and they would send it to the battalion commander, and also the commander of the Military District, and all other instances that had to be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's test that assertion of yours because you keep repeating that, Mr. Lausic. If we can go back then, and let's actually test your theory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to -- if we can go to P979, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is it from the 12th of August, and can you flip through this at will, Mr. Lausic. But let's take a look at the first two pages. They're pretty much the same substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll down in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, for example, the Zadar Company: A total of 49 persons were admitted at the collection centre for prisoners of war following operative processing; zero persons were taken back to the reception centre; 4 are undergoing medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page, please. The Croatian as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "In Sibenik, there are present a total of 25 persons, members of enemy formations at the collection centre for prisoners of war." Goes on and on and. The last paragraph under Sibenik: "There are still only five persons in the reception centre for civilians." If we can go to Sinj, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Scroll down in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "In the course of August 11, 11 new prisoners were brought to the prisoner of war collection centre in Sinj." This is it what Mr. Glavan is generally reporting about is prisoners of war, and now you keep trying to make the contention that somehow the crime section of the 72nd MP would put information in a daily report to the Split Military District Command, so let's take a look at the 12th of August, which is the date of this report and see what exactly, what kind of information was going in these daily reports that you keep referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Registrar, if we could have 65 ter 6984, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Daily report: "On the 12th of August, Zadar military police received" -- sorry, Zadar VP with the number received a report from a Mr. Vidaic a waiter in a restaurant in Zadar. That one member of the HV is pulling a gun on the guests in restaurants. Describes in great detail what they did. They identified the soldier, again in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In Split, this is point 2, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the next page in the English. Sorry, page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: A second incident -- if we can turn the page in Croatian as well, please. On the 12th of August in Split, the Split VP received a report from Miletic that there had been some shooting by HV members at Obalak Kineza Domogoja [phoen] Street in Split. Someone was sent down to do a report. Some guns were taken out, Zippo lighters. The next entry is: Breaches of provisions of the rules on military discipline for the 12th of August, no events recorded. Other incidents. Is there anything here that catches your eye, Mr. Lausic, about what General Gotovina learned on the 12th of August from a daily report, shooting in Split, intimidation in a restaurant in Zadar. There is no information in these reports about prisoners of war being processed. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the processing of prisoners of war does not fall under the heading of crime. If a prisoner of war, after being processed was tried -- was actually charged because they were grounds to suspect that he had committed the crime of armed rebellion that then would constitute a crime. But this is a standard report on the sort of incidents that have to do with grounds to suspect is that someone has commit at crime. Whether members of the Croatian military are perpetrators or victims. Mr. Glavan's report which you showed me is report dealing exclusively with the reception and processing of prisoner of war, which he did together with his colleagues from the Ministry of Interior. And it was delivered also to the military crime police department of the 72nd MP Battalion because they investigate these people, but it would not be reported under the heading of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We agree 100 percent on that, Mr. Lausic, and the only reason I brought this issue up right now is because it was you who said that this type of information that was in Mr. Glavan's report would have gone to the crime section of the battalion and then would have been reported in the daily report to the Split Military District Command. Now, I have all the daily reports that were sent to the Split Military District Command for the months of August and September; and at a later point in my examination we will go through all of those reports and we'll see exactly what type of information the military police was sending to the Split Military District command. But I can tell you, and Mr. Tieger will correct me if I'm wrong, the substance of the reports isn't much different than what we have seen on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know if this is part of the bar table submission or not, but I would tender this, if it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it is part of the bar table submission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then no objections, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objections. Yes, thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could have Exhibit D794, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Lausic, we had that daily report on the screen. It would have been one of the normal jobs of the military police if there was a breach -- a noted breach of military discipline to include that in a report; right?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is, again, the notes of the meeting, the coordination meeting on the 3rd, that was held between the MUP and the military police administration that you've referred to earlier today in your testimony. And let me call your attention to the -- to page 3 in the English, please. And page 2 in the Croatian. Now, these are the words that are ascribed to you, Mr. Lausic, and it says -- that's the bottom -- no, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry it is the bottom of page 2, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says: "Major-General Mate Lausic" -- you have it in front of you, Mr. Lausic?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do thank you. I have my document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Major-General Mate Lausic emphasised that the main negative experiences noted in Operation Flash were the following: "Lack of energy the military police activities, lack of coordination (in terms of dynamics and distribution of forces) under specific conditions on the ground, which reduced efficiency and unnecessarily created the illusion that the number of members engaged was insufficient. He also emphasised that he had now authorised UVP officers to replace the commanders of military police units on the spot, should they notice any irregularities in their work." That sentence relates to your prior order where you appointed Major Juric, Mr. Kozic, I think Mr. Cvitanovic; and in that order you said he is authorised to undertake all measures to ensure efficient and effective implementation of military police tasks in the 72nd and north operative zones of responsibility. And when you wrote that, "all measures," you clarified at the meeting on the 3rd that all measures meant they could even replace commanders of military units if necessary to get the job done; correct? I'm sorry, military police units. He could replace commanders of military units, if necessary, in order to get the job done.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can go back to D269, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, we would have to deal with two matters. I don't know what would be a suitable time, but I would certainly not have a break not later than ten minutes from now. And I take it that the issues would take five to seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I hope less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You hope less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. D269.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, again this is it the document we saw yesterday on your order on the work of the military police. And if we turn the page in English, please, and in Croatian. Now, do you agree with me that General Gotovina was not in your chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that no member of the armed forces -- I'm sorry, of the -- from the Main Staff, in the line of the Main Staff, meaning the Main Staff, Military Districts, and subordinate units were present at the meeting between Minister Jarnjak and Minister Susak or the subsequent working meeting between yourself and Mr. Moric, where some details were worked out on security measures on the eve of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The people from the same profession met to discuss the most efficient manner of carrying out the tasks which they were duty-bound under the law to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So the methods that you had agreed, because no military person was in your line of command, the only way to implement what was agreed upon at the meeting on the 3rd with Mr. Moric was through your line as the chief of the military police administration. Either that or you would have to ask somebody in the military line to follow your suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit I again fail to understand your question. Could you be more specific please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: General Gotovina, specifically here, and let me give you a concrete example. Whatever you and Mr. Moric agreed upon on the 3rd of August, in terms of methods, tactics, General Gotovina had no obligation to implement what you had agreed upon; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obligation referred to those who are authorised to act, and they were military and civilian policemen, based on the powers given to them by the law. General Gotovina was not a member of the military police and did not have the legal powers. It's well-known what the authorisation is given by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He did not have the legal powers to do what?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. The meeting was a meeting of men from the same profession: military police, civilian police. At the meeting, based on experience from Operation Flash, where certain irregularities had been observed, a plan was drawn up as to how to act most efficiently, both by the military and the civilian police, with the men and resources available on the territory we were to act on. After the meeting, I asked the chief of the MP administration sent to the MP units of the military police their duties; and these are contained in the points of those orders, and the same was done by Mr. Moric in his instructions to the chiefs of the police administrations. My order was sent to the commanders of the Military Districts for their information, so that they would know what the battalions, who were under their daily operative command, would be doing, what sort of methods and tactics they would be using. So they were provided with this information, so that they would be aware of what the police would be doing and where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Final question before the break. So you had command over the military police before and during Storm in order to issue such orders; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I commanded the military police for 12 years: Five years in wartime and seven in peacetime. And I issued hundreds of orders like this one, either to do with operations such as Maslenica, Bijesak, Oluja to liberate territory or dozens of other operative actions such as those mentioned yesterday, Varivode and so on. It was always through orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's now a good time for a break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First we'll deal with the two outstanding matters. But, Mr. Lausic, I don't know whether you get coffee or tea but you're already allowed to follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back in approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there were two issues. It's not entirely clear whether and to what extent they are related. The first one being the relevance of a question whether Mr. Lausic felt obliged to give his notebook to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the second one is that you would like have a look at the original of the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think the second one would be easier. I would like to have a look at the original notebook for 1995. My proposal would be that Mr. Lausic retrieve the diary, and if he has any concern about personal information that that submitted to the Chamber to review whether there is something really personal in there that -- that should be protected. I have no desire to go into anything that is truly personal. On the other hand, where he was at specific points of time that aren't necessarily -- there may be personal views -- at a birthday party in Knin on the 5th might be relevant, even though it is a personal matter. So something for the Chamber to review.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll further inquire with Mr. Lausic whether he is willing to -- And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The second issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course practically -- let me see then. We would then. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That might be a private session issue. I'm not sure if Mr. Tieger wants to move into private session or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I imagine we could deal with it otherwise, but it would be more awkward and probably pointless. I share the private session suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was still busy with the practicalities of the first, which is not necessary to be dealt in private session. The Chamber is supposed to look at portions of the notebook that are not transcribed to see whether they're private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's true, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm a very practical person; I don't know the word for birthday in B/C/S, Mr. Misetic. So, therefore, then, of course, perhaps you will have to do that with the assistance of a language assistant, something like that, that we are -- get a provisional impression of what is in the portions that are not transcribed. Now that's one. We then also have to compare exactly what is transcribed and not transcribed. I've got no idea whether it is every page, five birthdays or; so let's further inquire with the witness what portions approximately will not have been transcribed and to what extent he is willing to give access to it. Then we now turn into private session for the relevance issue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll have a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Lausic, would you be willing to -- to give the original version of your -- of your personal notes, to give it for inspection to the parties, and where you feel that matters of a personal nature are included, which you would not like to share with the parties in these proceedings, that we would have two copies: One complete copy, and perhaps the original that, of course, would then be returned to you; and a copy you prepare taking out the private matters, and then that the Chamber would just verify and can confirm to the parties that what you left out, that that is of a private character; so to give the full text, preferably the original to the Chamber, and to prepare a copy, taking out anything you consider personal. The Chamber will then verify whether the portions taken out are of a personal nature, and then confirm that to the parties, and the parties will then accept that these are -- that the Chamber verified that. Are you willing to cooperate in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, as photocopied pages of those parts, which were certified when making an additional copy. That is to say, the entries without the private matters blanked out and the copies without those parts. That is what was seen by the notary public who certified that those pages are, indeed, the pages of my diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But would you be willing to give the diary in its entirety and then exclusively to the Chamber, so that the Chamber verifies and confirms to the parties that everything you took out is, and will not then go into any further detail, is of a private nature. So that to provide the full -- if possible, the original, but if not, then at least a full photocopy of every page without blanked out anything. So for to us say, Okay that's true, this is a birthday or that's a funeral or -- and then one remaining issue. Sometimes if you may have described matters of a perfectly private nature, such as attending a wedding of a -- of someone you know well in Sarajevo, for example, that then what is private is why you were in Sarajevo. Nevertheless, the fact that you were in Sarajevo can have some relevance. If there's any information which the Chamber considers could have some relevance, apart from the personal page that of the occasion, then we might put that to you and say ask you whether you consider it private, that you were present at a certain day in Sarajevo or in Zagreb or in Belgrade or whatever. That's -- we would then verify that with you first. Would that be a practical solution? And would you be willing to give the original, which will be returned to you without -- it will be kept under the control of the Chamber but then it also gives an opportunity to verify whether the copied pages are fully consistent with the original. Yes? Then we'll take care that you'll be approached by the victims and witness section for the practical arrangements in relation to this. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. Those documents are in Zagreb. Technically that can be dealt with the Office of The Hague Tribunal in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the victims and witness section will then contact the outreach office in Zagreb, and we will find a practical solution for that. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, let me take you to Exhibit D844, which is another order of yours. Mr. Lausic, this is an order of yours at the back it says -- on the last page the date it was received is 4 August. So it's some time on or before the 4th of August, but there's no date in the caption. And it's an order from you that goes to the MP 3rd Company Detachment, Zadar; the 4th Company, Sibenik; and the 6th Company, Dubrovnik, attention to the commanders of those companies directly from you. And it's -- you're issuing an order on what the content of reports should be, and the preamble says: "With the view of uniform contents of reports on tasks, performance in the areas of responsibility, the reports should be submitted at time and in a way prescribed by point 12 of the above mentioned order ..." And we have already seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, if I'm correct on the date ... and then we go through the contents. And if we go to paragraph 2, which is the next page in English. I am sorry, the next page in English. We're on the same page in B/C/S, page 1. If we could zoom in on paragraph 2 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now you're ordering that -- the reports contain information on: "The status of public law and order in a zone of combat operations and in newly liberated areas, stating events when the military police had to act and the results of the intervention." Point 3 is about safety and military road traffic. Point 4 is the status of crime in liberated areas and in zones of combat operations. The number of crimes, the crime reports filed, and the escort of HV members who committed a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page in Croatian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Number 5, you want information on the number of arrested persons sorted by time when they were taken over from HV units, the time of handing them over to a reception centre, the number of civilians, women and children, and the elderly handed over to the police units of the MUP. Point 6 is about information on search results of territory and facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we scroll down to point 9 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The system of daily reporting through services remains as it is. This report is to be signed by a MP unit commander, that is, officers of the military police administration in accordance with the item 12 of the above mentioned order ..." And it's signed. Now, this is the information that the military police units within the 72nd and the 73rd had to submit to Major Juric so that he could prepare his reports in time to send them to you by 8.00 every night; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must confess that this is the first time I see the order. This was a coded order. I would like to see the original, based on which the encryption centre coded it. Although it says in the signature block chief, Chief Major-General Ante [sic] Lausic. I believe it was signed by Major Juric. It would have been unusual for me as the chief of the administration to direct company -- to contact company commanders directly. I'm afraid I cannot state anything about the document, without being able to see the original rather than this coded copy. Only after I see whose signature there is, could I tell you whether it was indeed Major Juric who signed it as the commander of the forward command post of the MP administration according to the powers he received from me pursuant to my order. In that case, he was able to issue orders such as this one to the respective companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me break that apart. First, there is no question that you in fact did have the authority to issue an order directly to a company; correct? If you chose to do so?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be unusual. My orders were sent to battalion commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Whether unusual or not, again, my question is: There is no question that you had the authority to issue an order directly to a company; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But I have to repeat, it would have been highly unusual. I can't imagine what reasons there may have been for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in terms of content of the reports, this is the information that you wanted in the reports that were going to be sent to you from Major Juric; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If this was signed by Major Juric, pursuant to my authorisation, then he wanted to have the information referred to in the order so that he could send a report to the administration in keeping with my order of the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. My question is very specific. Whether it was issued by you -- it is at least appears on its face to have been issued by you. But even if it was issued by Major Juric, let's put that aside for a minute. You wanted in those reports that would come to you the information that is it outlined in this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And this is the type of information that would have gone to Major Juric pursuant to your order, and then to you, and there was no provision that these orders -- I'm sorry, these reports would be copied to the Split Military District Command; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we focus on the last paragraph of this order irrespective of the fact whether it was me or Juric who signed it, it says that the system of daily reporting through duty offices remains the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And we've seen one such daily report, and if you want me to show you the daily reports from the 4th and 5th, as I told you before, we can talk about drunk soldiers and traffic accidents in the daily reports; that's not what I'm actually talking about. The specific content that you ordered that -- to be prepared about all the different areas of information you were seeking, those reports would only go to the military police administration, and there was no order that said that they should be copied to the Split Military District Command. That's the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go back to page 1 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, if we can go to Exhibit D845, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is a report from the company commander of the 4th Company Sibenik to Major Budimir but in the preamble it says: "Pursuant to the oral order of the chief of the military police administration Major-General Mate Lausic, received 7 August 1995, at 1310 hours, who ordered that a security system be established urgently at the entries and exits of the following warehouses." And then it identifies the three warehouses. And it says: "The number of the personnel that will be necessary for the aforementioned security will be determined by the Commander Mihael Budimir or Captain Djulic." It should be Dzolic. Do you recall issuing an oral order to the company commander in Sibenik regarding the securing of warehouses on the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my notes -- or, rather, the copy of my notes, I do not have entries for the 7th of August. I would have to check that against the original. However, it is probably true what it says in the document, and that is that I had orally issued an order on the security of warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay, let me --

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I actually -- let me try to help you, because there is another document that may help refresh your recollection. And if I can show you D795, which is actually a written order issued by you to Major Juric about warehouses. This is the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll down to see ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the 7th of August, and you're invoking Article 8 of the rules and you order: "1, is to establish the location of every warehouse facility within the entire liberated territory. "2, is to evaluate a method of physically securing all warehouse facilities and establishing physical security of the mentioned facilities from 0000 to 2400 hours." Point 5 on the next page in English. It says: "The report on the implementation of this order to be delivered starting 7 August 1995 attached to the daily report submitted according to the military police administration order dated 2 August ..." So it's fair to say that you issued an order to Major Juric, this is an operational order; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably right after the oral order was received from Mr. Susak that MP units take over the security of all warehouses in the newly liberated area as issued to me, the reason being that those warehouses were being looted by HV members or that members of the central logistics base that was supposed to take over the warehouses were not granted access to those warehouses by the HV members who had occupied them. That is why the oral order was issued to me that the military police take over security of the warehouses. As stated in order, the entry to the premises and the issuing of materiel and technical equipment is not allowed without a written permission from Vladimir Zagorac. I provided an opinion in my two statements as a suspect and a witness upon being questioned by the investigator about whether the minister of defence, the military police was transferred from its general duties to provide security for the warehouses, which is certainly not something that would fall within the authority of the military police because these are not exactly rocket-launcher bases, if I may be a bit ironic. When I answered that question, I was of the view that, based on the information received by minister of defence that those warehouses were being looted and their contents taken away by various HV members, and that the employees of the 300th logistic base who according to a previous order were supposed to take over those warehouses but were not granted access, that is why he issued an order to me. Then as a follow-up, I first issued an oral and then a written order. I have an entry in my diary that I was told by Major Juric that on the 7th of August, at 2200 hours, the minister's order was implemented and the premises handed over to the logistics base as well as that the Golubic and Krka warehouse was being secured. The only one that was not secured was the third one because the 3rd Guards Brigade was billeted there. The next morning, Mr. Biskic, my deputy, informed me that the Slunj warehouse was taken over by the military police forces and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that you want to provide as much detail as possible. If I need very specific details about particular issues like which warehouses were or weren't secured, I will be sure to ask you a follow-up question. But if you could keep your answers focussed to the question that I posed, it will help us get through this material.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have on the screen Exhibit P2166, at English page 37 and B/C/S page 33, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is your diary entry for the 8th of August. I'm interested in the references to Major Juric at paragraphs 1 and 2. You referred to him as the commander of the forward command post 73rd VP and 72nd VP in Knin: "Is to carry out all military and police tasks in their zones of responsibility with the existing formations with additional military police administration forces." And point 2, second sentence is: "Review the possibility of having a part of the forces two or three groups deployed to the forward command post of the 72nd and 73rd Military Police Battalions in Knin and placed under the command of Major Juric to carry out tasks in their zone of responsibility." Now on the 8th of August, your commander for all intents and purposes in the field was Major Juric; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you use the phrase here: "He is to carry out all military and police tasks in the zone of responsibility with existing formations." That's correct as well.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, at least through Major Juric, and I asked you this question before the break and I will ask it again: Through Major Juric, who was your eyes and ears in the field, that was your way of maintaining command in the field, through him; correct?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have P2159, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which is your witness statement, Mr. Lausic. If you could turn your attention to paragraph 168 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, this is page 35 in the English version. And page 36 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let me first start off by noting that today when I started I asked you about the systemisation chart and about -- it said that the chief of the military police administration whether he was responsible for the work of the administration in the units in -- in 1995 and you said at page 6, beginning page 6 line 23 you agreed with me, that in fact systemisation never changed, and that you obviously, pursuant to the systemisation, were responsible for the work of the military police units. And just now you have acknowledged that you were in command through Major Juric. Now, your statement, at page 168 [sic] says: "One of the main tasks of the military police is to ensure and control the discipline of the military.
